title: Soothsayer, Worldmaker
subtitle: The goddess delights in toying with the piety of her believers.

trails.title: The Weaving of Shadows, Volume V
trails.description: The boundary shatters, and an astrologer glimpses an unspeakable truth.

items.text: Soothsayer, Worldmaker
On the stage, Octavia remains the picture of serenity as she orchestrates the congress.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Ms. Recoleta, as a witness to the congress, you have the right to express your doubts—calmly.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Listen, you—
She recalls the complaints of her two former companions, the jailer's dismissals, and the confused expressions of every editor she has ever faced.
If she were to lay out every detail of her novel here and now, she would only get the same response.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: *huff* No, it's nothing. It's just that I'd like to participate in the dice-rolling ceremony. May I?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Of course! The very fact that you're standing here in the Panopticon proves that you share a common fate with it.

Recoleta surveys the prisoners waiting to cast their die. Their expressions are serene, untroubled, calmly awaiting their fate. The joys and misfortunes of those before them do not affect the long, winding queue in the slightest.
She takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It doesn't matter when I roll the Die, since the rolls are simply a reflection of the randomness of fate, right?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Precisely.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Then, I'd like to perform my roll after the 27th inmate. Is that alright?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: As you wish, Ms. Recoleta.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: It seems fate favors you, Ms. Recoleta.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Here are your supplies.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Please be sure to follow the distribution rules of the congress. This is an essential structure of Comala and a belief shared by all its inmates. Honor it.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Just as I suspected.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: These supplies belong to me now, Octavia. I'm free to use them however I please.
Recoleta strides toward Edoardo, who has curled up in a distant corner, clutching his head, as his body trembles in silence.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Here, Edoardo, take them.

items.speaker: Inmate IV
items.text: B-But I haven't fulfilled my destiny yet.

items.speaker: Inmate IV
items.text: These precious tablets and capsules ... I can't accept them. They are gifts from fate. The Die has placed them in your palm.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: But I don't need them; you do.

items.speaker: Inmate IV
items.text: Th-Thank you, kind miss.
The prisoner's trembling stops. He blankly pinches his arm, as if trying to distinguish reality from dream.
Then, all at once, he snatches the medication from her hands and shoves it into his mouth.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Edoardo?! What's wrong? A-Are you taking the medicine right now?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: There's no need to rush. There's plenty of it. You can have it all.

items.speaker: Inmate I
items.text: For goodness' sake, Edoardo! How could you squander fate's gifts like this?

items.speaker: Inmate I
items.text: Kind miss, please, give me the medication. I need them more than anyone else.

items.speaker: Inmate II
items.text: No, I'm the one who needs them most. Give me the medication. I beg of you.

items.speaker: Inmate II
items.text: With the protection of these amulets, I might finally be able to get a peaceful night's sleep, no more trembling floors and wailing ghosts.
The prisoners shove and struggle, countless hands reaching toward the hapless writer, trying to snatch the small round pills of salvation.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Enough! Enough!!
A blue glow spreads through the room, forcing the prisoners to clutch their heads and fall down to their knees. Their riot comes to an abrupt halt.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: You shouldn't have done that, Ms. Recoleta.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Your ignorant generosity could shatter the very basis of our survival.
She steps toward Edoardo, now writhing in pain, and picks up a few stray capsules scattered at his feet.
The pills dissolve into a stream of voided sand, vanishing as it pours through her fingers.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: We have never had such chaos at the congress. Understand this: We rely only on the randomness of fate to distribute supplies and assign responsibilities.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: If you disrupt this status quo, the entire system of the Panopticon will collapse beyond repair.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: It is only by respecting the arbitrariness of fate and adhering to the rules of the Die of Babylon that we have kept this place functioning all this time.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: The Die of Babylon?!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Tell me, how did you know this name? Are you the one orchestrating this whole thing?
Recoleta, equally confused and furious, grabs the hostess's collar.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: C-Could it be? Are you Aleph, just as Vertin suspected?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Let go of me, Ms. Recoleta! Have you gone mad?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: The roll of the Die is absolutely random. I'm not orchestrating anything. Before the congress began, I made an oath. I intend to keep it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, calm down, Ms. Recoleta. I think she's telling the truth.
She lets go of her grip as the reality of their situation dawns on her.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: S-Sorry, Octavia, but, please, you have to tell me how you learned about the Die of Babylon.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I must know. Only my pen pal and I should have any knowledge about this die.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: I heard about it from the Physician. He described it as a symbol of collective consciousness that we could harness to maintain immaculate order in the Panopticon.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: The Comala Congress was coined, iterated, and perfected by the Physician based on this concept.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Physician again. Everything eventually leads back to him, just as we suspected.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I see.
Recoleta casts her eyes over to the silent jaguar, who has remained wordless from beginning to end, watching it all unfold.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Jailer, we have to meet with the Physician in person, now.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: As I've told you many times, Dr. Merlin is too busy at the moment.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I couldn't possibly trouble him over a novel and a pen pal. They're just fantasies.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Couldn't you make an exception?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What if they're not just fantasies? What if they're tied to the very survival of this place?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Recoleta said the Panopticon could collapse because of the Die of Babylon.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Are you seriously telling me you believe that nonsense?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It wasn't nonsense, nor are they fantasies! You saw with your own eyes how I won the die roll!

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: It was just a coincidence.
The jailer's words are at odds with the subtle motions of her eyes and face. The Foundation's investigators seize on a prime opportunity to apply pressure.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What if we present you with stronger evidence to prove it's more than just a coincidence?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If everything in the Panopticon proceeds according to Ms. Recoleta's novel, as she says, she should be able to predict what happens next.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Including the roll results of the "absolutely random" Die.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: That's right! The Die of Babylon isn't random at all. It's nothing but a supercilious fraud veiled under the guise of fate, an enactor of the inescapable loop of history, and—

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: And not one of you is paying attention to me whatsoever. Ugh, to hell with this era of ignoring unknown writers.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Recoleta, please make your prediction for the next inmate's die roll.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This way, you can prove to Ms. Jailer the irrefutable connection between Comala and your novel, The Rise and Fall of Sanity.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You finally remembered its name! Oh, what sweet balm to my spirit!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Octavia, please continue the congress, and let the next inmate perform their roll. Then Ms. Recoleta's statement will be proven true.
The hostess of the congress remains noncommittal.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: I appreciate the reminder. No matter the interruption, the Comala Congress must go on, though not for Ms. Recoleta's sake, of course.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Next inmate, please.
Following the die's designated order, the next prisoner steps forward to roll.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Hello, Inmate García. You know what to do.

items.speaker: García
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "The 6th face. A broken pillar. The conflux of fortune and calamity."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: So, the result of the next roll will be a 6.
Her prophetic precision plunges the Hall of New Encounters into breathless silence.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: As fate reveals, the number is 6.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Just as Ms. Recoleta predicted.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: That could still be a coincidence. Do it again.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "The 13th face. A bewildering cadenza lacking a true beginning or end."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "The 4th face. A drowning man used the last of his strength to swim to safety, only to discover he'd mistaken a mirror for the surface of the water."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "The 17th face. He limped toward the distant oasis, only for the faint moisture and eerie stillness to cruelly reveal it as a mirage."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "The 6th face. Another broken pillar, with identical cracks to the last. It confirmed the Paracausality Researcher's hypothesis—this place used to be a circular building."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Is that enough? I've almost finished the entire chapter.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: It's not possible.
One "coincidence" after another begins to stir into an uproar.
The coincidences appear endless.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Who are you?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I'm sorry if this comes as a shock to you, but I did warn you, Octavia.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Now, it's proven. The Die of Babylon is anything but the so-called "randomness of fate."

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Have you been sent here by some god, or are you a Hopi prophet?

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: Have you brought this knowledge to save us, or to shatter our beliefs, our world?
A question destined never to need an answer. She lets her eyes fall into the cardboard box and onto the twenty-sided die. The ridiculousness of its nature becomes starkly visible.

items.speaker: Octavia
items.text: What is this thing in my hand? What are we? What is this prison?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I don't know if it's some kind of sorcery or arcane skill, but it's unfathomable.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I'll take you to the Physician. Not because of your earlier request, but because the situation has escalated beyond my means.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: The overseer of the Panopticon will decide how to handle your situation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: To be honest, Ms. Recoleta. I wasn't sure you'd be able to correctly predict everything.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, are you saying that you risked everything on a hunch?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It worked, didn't it?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Come with me. Dr. Merlin's office is in the central tower.
For her part, the now vindicated writer follows at the end of the line, letting her mind race like a bullet train.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: In the sixth version of my novel, everyone in the town dies because of the Die of Babylon, for only death can close the loop of history.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: And Jailer, you're the Bank Clerk, right?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: So, in the end, will you also have a meltdown, like the Bank Clerk does, when he realizes that he and the Dune Piscator are the same person?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: If all of this is tied to The Rise and Fall of Sanity, then, as its creator ...

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I will get to the bottom of this.
